subject: Latency targets and hybrid deployment options — ClearForm discovery recap
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.inference.com>
To: Ashley Park <ashley@clearform.com>, Ben Zhou <ben.zhou@clearform.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.inference.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com
Date: Thu, 10 Oct 2029 16:15:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + latency/throughput asks from today

Hi Ashley / Ben —

Thanks for the time today. Below is a short recap of the technical items we discussed and proposed next steps so your engineering and procurement teams have one place to reference. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain and goals we heard
- Real-time document enrichment at 99th percentile conversational latency of <=200ms for 512-token responses (p95 target tighter, p99 is the hard constraint).
- Current system will require burstable throughput up to ~250 rps during morning peaks, sustained 120 rps average.
- Data residency concerns for PII; ClearForm prefers private VPC deployment for inference with a Redwood Private control plane.

Model & inference constraints
- Primary model candidate: Llama2-70B (quantized variant) for quality; fallback to Llama2-13B for cost-sensitive routes.
- Typical generation length expected 200-600 tokens; we should validate KV-cache memory needs with a 1k-window stress test.

Topology options we sketched
- Hybrid Private: dedicated GPU pool in your GCP VPC with Redwood Private control plane for orchestration.
- Canary plan: start with n1-standard reserved capacity for baseline (8xA100 equivalent) -> ramp to autoscale groups with burst capacity on hosted nodes.

Short technical asks (for your team)
1) Confirm peak/session concurrency assumptions (you gave 3–4k concurrent active users during peak).
2) Share a sanitized sample payload size distribution and typical prompt context length.
3) Procurement contact for POC SOW and expected payment terms.

Attachments: I attached a draft SLO matrix and the topology sketch we drew on the call. Also attaching a POC quote for an initial 2-week validation.

Next steps (proposed)
- Redwood: produce two deployment sketches (fully private, hybrid with hosted fallback), updated SLO matrix with cost estimates, and baseline test plan by Monday 10/14.
- ClearForm: confirm sample payloads and procurement contact by end of week.

Thanks again — I looped in Rishi and Karthik for the follow-up on autoscaling and kernel selection.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks Mina — this is great and aligns with our internal notes. A couple quick clarifications from engineering here:

- When you say p95 <=200ms and p99 hard constraint, can you sketch the degradation curve you expect if we hit 300–400ms? Specifically: error budget behavior and whether Redwood will route to fallback model automatically vs. returning a slower response.
- For KV-cache sizing: do you have an example mapping of token window -> DRAM/GPU memory for Llama2-70B quantized? We need that to approve our infra reservations.

Procurement is looped on this thread (procurement@clearform.com). Ben, can you add anything about internal SSO/KMS requirements?

Ashley
Director of Product
ClearForm Labs

Appreciate the detailed summary. From an infra perspective: a few specifics that will determine capacity and topology choices

- SSO & KMS: ClearForm uses Okta SSO and AWS KMS for key management for production secrets. We will need Redwood Private to integrate with our KMS and avoid egressing unencrypted request payloads to hosted nodes.
- Expected payload sizes: average request payload ~6KB, 95th percentile 28KB (includes embedded user metadata).
- Tolerance: for some endpoints (real-time enrichment) users expect sub-200ms p95; for non-interactive batch jobs 1–2s is acceptable. So route-level SLOs matter.

If Redwood can provide a suggested degradation policy (e.g., degrade to Llama2-13B for non-critical routes, or gracefully drop long-context tokens), we can sign off faster.

Ben
CTO, ClearForm Labs

Hi Ashley / Ben —

Thanks — noted. Quick answers inline and a clear set of follow-ups so procurement/engineering can proceed.

On p95/p99 degradation behaviour
- Recommended policy: Redwood will attempt low-latency routing first. If SLOs breach, automated fallback paths are: 1) route to a lower-cost smaller model variant (13B quantized) for non-critical routes, 2) enable prefix/KV cache hits to short-circuit repeated context, 3) if GPU pool exhausted, spill to hosting nodes in the same region with strict rate limiting. We can codify route-level policies for each API endpoint.

On KV-cache sizing (quick heuristic)
- For Llama2-70B quantized with 1k-window: expect ~14–18 GiB of KV per 2048-token chunk of cached context when using our optimized KV packing. We'll run a memory sweep during the POC against your representative payloads and share exact numbers.

POC / next-step checklist
1) Redwood to run two baseline synthetic tests next week against a copy of your payload distribution: lower-latency profile (p95 target 180ms) and throughput profile (sustained 120 rps, bursts to 250 rps).
2) Redwood to ship a short SOW and POC SOW (attached redwood-poc-quote.pdf) for 2-week validation in your VPC.
3) ClearForm to confirm procurement contact and KMS ownership (procurement@clearform.com looped).

I'll assign Rishi to own the test plan and Karthik to prepare kernel/quantization recommendations once we see the sample payloads. Expect the test plan and a refined SLO matrix by 10/14.

If procurement is ready we can start onboarding next week.

Best,
Mina
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
